physical.notes: The manual establishes the single memory target. This is the canonical Neo visible sw11p target center; its overlapping DropTrigger is the controller sensor and the adjacent center-lock magnet remains a separate assembly.

The official manual proves the physical trough order. Neo exposes only the trough-out kicker, so the older table's five-position chain is translated into the canonical Neo frame by aligning its switch-22 kicker with Neo BallRelease at (0.849790, 0.906658). Preserve the proven v1.10 initial controller state of 19-22 occupied and 18 clear.

mechanisms.behavior: The physical trough uses position switches 18-21 and jam opto 22. The known-working script initializes four balls on switches 19-22, leaving leftmost switch 18 clear, and output 1 ejects from the right end.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: Output 2 launches a ball resting at shooter-lane switch 23. The working table uses power 52 with random variation 3.
mechanisms.label: Auto launcher

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 10 stays active with a captured ball. Output 55 rotates the two-way VUK/deflector; output 6 then ejects along the selected path. The working table's standard path uses direction 85 degrees, force 38, and Z 100.
mechanisms.label: Left eject and rotating VUK

mechanisms.behavior: Output 4 raises and output 5 lowers the single memory target. Switch 11 is active while down; a ball held behind it is released when the target rises.
mechanisms.label: Center memory drop target

mechanisms.behavior: Output 3 is a PWM-capable magnet behind the memory target. The working table uses a centered capture field of radius 135 and permits multiple-ball capture; switches 33 and 34 track balls in the center lock lane.
mechanisms.label: Center magnet lock

mechanisms.behavior: PWM output 53 drives the ship down and into a shake/crash phase; output 56 releases or restores its latch, and switch 53 reports the crashed/latched state. Output 7 fires the captured ball back at super speed. The working animation advances at 100 Hz through down steps 2-50, shake steps 101-154, and return steps 201-250.
mechanisms.label: Animated Vengeance battleship

mechanisms.behavior: Outputs 51 and 52 independently control the left and right orbit gates; switches 52 and 51 respectively report ball travel through the adjacent orbits.
mechanisms.label: Left and right orbit control gates

mechanisms.behavior: Output 54 returns a ball entering right-drain switch 44. Do not confuse it with output 7, which is the Vengeance super-speed kickback.
mechanisms.label: Bottom drain kickback

mechanisms.behavior: Lower outputs 15/16 use buttons 84/82 and normally-closed EOS inputs 83/81. Upper-right output 12 uses dedicated button 86.
mechanisms.label: Three flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Switches 30, 31, and 32 pulse outputs 9, 10, and 11 respectively.
mechanisms.label: Three pop bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Output 22 runs the playfield laser-projector motor. It has no controller-facing position switch in the manual or working table.
mechanisms.label: Laser projector

The service drawing places the physical laser motor beneath the lower-left apron. The coordinate is a calibrated manual projection with practical uncertainty of about plus or minus 0.04 normalized x and 0.03 y; full-table laser render fields are not physical motor locations.

The proven v1.10 script establishes output 31's Vengeance-flasher semantics through its F31/F31a render helpers. The Neo table maps the same output to VengFlashGI, whose light center supplies this rest-state parent-relative assembly point; the broad F31/F31a bloom geometry is excluded.
SAM_FASTFLIPSOL synthetic state used for low-latency flipper gating; not a physical I/O Power Driver transistor.

The official page-152 drawing establishes 27 wedge-base sockets, four bayonet sockets, and three illuminated pop-bumper assemblies: 34 playfield emitters total on physical GI0/GI1/GI3 wiring regions. Individual base and wiring-region assignments are not asserted in placement IDs because the drawing does not support a fully reliable per-socket transcription. Its separate backbox inset proves four white GI3, two blue GI1, and one red GI0 bayonet, bringing the physical aggregate to 41 emitters behind PinMAME's one GI-0 transport channel. The 31 drawn socket centers are calibrated manual projections: their socket identity and physical region are validated, but the drawing does not support a quantified per-socket positional tolerance and the six-decimal values must not be read as sub-object measurement precision. The three pop points are canonical Neo assembly centers. The seven backbox fixtures are inventoried here but intentionally have no playfield-space placement. All VPX bloom, reflection, and Laser* helpers are excluded.
